name: Search bar filters products by model name and asserts the result set actually narrows

steps.script: (() => { const cards = document.querySelectorAll('.cat-product-grid .card'); const named = Array.from(cards).filter(c => (c.querySelector('.card-name')?.textContent || '').trim().length > 0); return { dataLoaded: named.length === cards.length && cards.length > 0, total: cards.length }; })()
steps.description: Wait until cards have populated names (not skeleton)
Click the search input field in the catalog
steps.snapshotHint: Look for an input with placeholder containing 'search' or the search icon button

steps.description: Type a product name in the search field

steps.script: (() => { const cards = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('.cat-product-grid .card')); const names = cards.map(c => (c.querySelector('.card-name')?.textContent || '').trim()); const allMatch = names.length > 0 && names.every(n => n.toLowerCase().includes('iphone')); return { count: cards.length, names, allMatch }; })()
steps.description: After typing 'iPhone' the catalog must show only iPhone-named cards (and at least 1)

steps.script: (() => { const inputs = document.querySelectorAll('input[type="text"], input[type="search"], input:not([type])'); for (const input of inputs) { if ((input.placeholder || '').toLowerCase().includes('search') || input.value === 'iPhone') { const nativeInputValueSetter = Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(window.HTMLInputElement.prototype, 'value').set; nativeInputValueSetter.call(input, ''); input.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', { bubbles: true })); input.dispatchEvent(new Event('change', { bubbles: true })); break; } } return { cleared: true }; })()

steps.description: After clearing the search the catalog returns to >= 2 cards

businessContext: Search is the primary way customers find specific phones — broken search means browsing friction. This version asserts (a) result set narrows to only matching names and (b) clearing the search restores the full list.
